name: IL-10
label: Safe D

Incumbent Brad Schneider running with a large financial advantage ($3.0M raised, $1.7M on hand)

model.rationale: Schneider holds a +12 Democratic district with a decisive money edge, while Lambrecht shows no visible fundraising or outside support; markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-implied margin with only a modest discount for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race, or a major shift in the national environment toward Republicans, would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Brad Schneider, the Democratic incumbent in Illinois' 10th District, seeks another term in a seat that leans about twelve points Democratic at the baseline. He has raised roughly $3 million and holds $1.7 million on hand, while Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising figures and no outside groups are active in the race on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. Prediction markets give Schneider about a 96% chance of winning. Everything points to a comfortable incumbent victory, with the only meaningful uncertainty being how a strong Republican national environment might compress the margin in an otherwise safe Democratic seat.
